text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. However, most APIs require authentication, such as an API key or token, to verify who you are. You must also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, good error handling is important, because requests can fail for many reasons, and your program should respond gracefully.
